title: the Weeping Wood Rising Anew
premise: Wendell Yarrow, exiled for a storm-calling that killed her brother, has hidden among charm-sellers in the magic-outlawed city of Greyhollow. When her date, cartographer Ivo Senn, discovers their meeting inscribed in a century-old prophecy book, they learn the 'Weeping Wood' — a sentient forest that devours memories — has been wearing the king as a puppet and will consume the city's collective past at the next eclipse. To unbind him, Wendell must reclaim the storm magic she swore off and offer the Wood her most painful memory in trade. In the end she frees the king but loses her memory of her brother; Ivo and her found family of charm-sellers vow to remember him for her, and together they begin rebuilding a city where magic is no longer a crime.
about_author: Paloma Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing oral histories from coastal villages before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about grief, weather, and the families we choose, and lives near a forest she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Charms for a City That Forgot
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She sells a luck-knot to a frightened baker, hiding her true power behind trinkets, then meets Ivo Senn for a first date at a night market. The emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by cautious hope, undercut by the guilt she carries about her exile.

chapters.title: The Book That Knew Tonight
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In his map shop he finds a prophecy folio describing tonight's date word for word, ending with a line about 'the weeping wood rising anew.' Wendell recognizes the sigil of the royal house. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as fate intrudes on something tender.

chapters.title: Greyhollow's Long Silence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They seek out Mother Quill, leader of the charm-sellers' underground, who reveals the Wood took the real king three years ago — the same year Wendell was exiled. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure, and the sting of learning her banishment was orchestrated.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The pair travels to the Weeping Wood's edge, where trees drip with stolen memories; Ivo glimpses his dead mother's last day and nearly loses himself. Emotional beat: seduction of the past, and the first understanding that memory can be both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The King Who Is Not a King
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They infiltrate the palace during a masque and confirm the crowned figure is hollow, animated by root and sap. Wendell's storm magic stirs involuntarily, nearly exposing them. Emotional beat: terror and resolve — she cannot stay hidden much longer.

chapters.title: Roots in Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Mother Quill's POV. Backstory unfolds: the Wood was once a guardian spirit driven mad when the crown outlawed magic and burned its grove; it now hoards memories to fill its emptiness. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster, and the group fracturing over whether to destroy or heal it.

chapters.title: The Eclipse Bargain
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Wood offers a trade through a dream: the king freed in exchange for Wendell's worst memory — the storm that killed her brother. Ivo begs her to refuse. Emotional beat: agonizing choice between selfhood and duty, love and penance.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller, Unbound
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the eclipse, Wendell calls a true storm for the first time since her exile, tearing the roots from the crown while Ivo anchors her to the present by reciting every detail of their date. Emotional beat: fury, grief, and fierce trust fused into one act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Price of Rising
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The king wakes; the Wood, unburdened, begins to heal into a guardian again — but Wendell's memory of her brother is gone, leaving a blank ache. Emotional beat: hollow victory, mourning someone she can no longer name, held up by Ivo and the charm-sellers.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Spring comes to Greyhollow; the repeal of the magic ban begins, the restored king plants a new grove, and the found family records Wendell's brother's story so she can learn him again. Emotional beat: quiet hope — identity rebuilt not from what was lost, but from who chooses to stay.
